content:
nina: quick flag  ran a routine compare bringing up rerank-lite-int8 and seeing MRR@10 degrade vs fp16 while NDCG@10 ticked up. small but reproducible. anyone seen this pattern before?

omar: paste numbers pls

nina: fp16 (prod model): NDCG@10=0.658, MRR@10=0.426. int8: NDCG@10=0.667, MRR@10=0.405. seeds=40/41/42, holdout=holdout-mar-2026, topk=50.

lucy: magnitude similar across seeds?

nina: yes, stdev ~0.002 on NDCG, ~0.005 on MRR.

aditya: before blaming quant, check data pipeline parity. our eval harness uses candidate list exported from yesterday, prod uses new dedupe+normalize rules (release 2026-03-10). That can change which doc occupies top1.

lucy: also tokenizer could be off. int8 runtime uses tokenization micro-optimized path that defaults to preserve_case=false for perf. fp16 harness used preserve_case=true historically. top1 sensitive to case.

qa: quick checklist: candidate snapshot, tokenizer config, priming/truncation, and scoring thresholds. small differences can flip exact-match metrics.

nina: agreed. plan: run three ablations and one combined run: (A) candidate parity (use prod snapshot cs-2026-03-11), (B) tokenizer parity (force prod-tokenizer.json), (C) priming/truncation parity (prod-priming.json), (D) all parity. I'll run seeds 40..42 for each.

omar: add an overlap metric in outputs: top1_overlap_rate and token_count_delta_fraction.

aditya: add command template to keep runs consistent:
```
python -m eval.runner
  --model rerank-lite-int8
  --holdout holdout-mar-2026
  --seeds 40,41,42
  --candidates cs-2026-03-11
  --tokenizer prod-tokenizer.json
  --priming prod-priming.json
  --out outputs/3305009999_ablationA.json
```

infra-bot: eval job queued: eval-3305009999-A by nina on runner-eval-7

nina: starting ablation A (candidate parity). interim log:
```
[INFO] seed=40 model=rerank-lite-int8 NDCG@10=0.668 MRR@10=0.412 p@1=0.288
[INFO] seed=40 model=rerank-lite-fp16 NDCG@10=0.658 MRR@10=0.426 p@1=0.303
```

lucy: what's top1 overlap cnt?

nina: overlap report: overall candidate pool overlap 99.1%, top1 id changed for 1.9% of queries after normalization. token_count_delta_fraction=0.05 (5% queries changed token counts).

aditya: that 1.9% could explain a non-trivial part of MRR drop. are those brand / exact-match cases?

nina: sampling says lots are brand-explicit queries where URL normalization merged multiple SERP entries.

infra-bot: eval job queued: eval-3305009999-B (tokenizer parity)

nina: ablation B (tokenizer parity) results:
```
ablation B (prod-tokenizer forced): avg NDCG@10=0.665 avg MRR@10=0.418 p@1=0.296
```

lucy: tokenizer parity moved MRR closer to fp16 but not entirely.

aditya: run C (priming parity) next. set truncation and prefix exactly as prod.

infra-bot: eval job queued: eval-3305009999-C (priming parity)

nina: ablation C results:
```
ablation C (prod-priming only): avg NDCG@10=0.661 avg MRR@10=0.414 p@1=0.294
```

omar: priming helps a bit, but seems candidates + tokenizer are heavier contributors. run D (all parity).

infra-bot: eval job queued: eval-3305009999-D (all parity)

nina: full parity run finished:
```
full parity (candidates+tokenizer+priming) avg NDCG@10=0.665 avg MRR@10=0.423 p@1=0.302
```

lucy: that basically closes the MRR gap to <0.5% vs fp16. conclusion: harness mismatches (candidate normalization + tokenization + priming) were majority cause. int8 scoring distribution slightly different but not the dominant factor.

aditya: action items:
- nina: add candidate-snapshot id and normalization version to eval metadata by default
- lucy: add tokenizer parity unit to onboard tests for new models (fail if token_count_delta_fraction > 1%)
- omar: coordinate a 0.5% online canary with fallback-to-fp16 on top1 mismatches for 30m to give product confidence

qa: note for docs: when onboarding quantized variants, require an "eval parity" checklist covering candidate pool, tokenizer, priming, and seed reproducibility.

nina: created ticket INF-4402 and attached run artifacts outputs/3305009999-full.json.

infra-bot: INF-4402 updated with artifact outputs/3305009999-full.json


(ends)
